name: Odwa Dilizo
qualifications: LLB, Certificate in Advanced Corporate Law and Securities Law, Certificate in Compliance Management, PGD BA
membership: Legal Practice Council, Association of Arbitrators (Southern Africa) NPC
projects: Project representative and legal advisor to the PropWatch and PropSol joint ventures.
bio: Odwa holds an LLB from Nelson Mandela University and is admitted as an attorney of the High Court of South Africa. He has also completed a postgraduate diploma in business management, and is currently training in dispute resolution for the construction industry.

He spent five years as head of the land acquisition team and legal expert to the land-legal team for the Greater Edendale and Vulindlela Development Initiative, the inter-governmental programme to redevelop Edendale in Pietermaritzburg, and served as property manager for the MAJV, the GeoAfrika-led property portfolio service provider to SANRAL, covering property management, identification and acquisition.

Odwa’s work is largely in public law: assisting municipalities with land tenure and the acquisition of land in urban, rural and tribal areas for large-scale developments, and drafting agreements, policies and guidelines for state-owned enterprises. He is the service providers’ representative for the PropWatch and PropSol joint ventures’ contracts with SANRAL.

name: Karl Hoffmann
qualifications: BA, LLB, Conveyancer, Mediation Foundation Training
bio: Karl holds a Bachelor of Arts and a Bachelor of Laws from Rhodes University, and is an admitted attorney and conveyancer of the High Court of South Africa.

He joined HSG in 2014 and is a director and head of the conveyancing department. His work is largely project-related conveyancing in the public and private sectors: he has acted as the appointed conveyancer for low-income government housing developments, private gated estates, and sectional-title conversions and developments, and has handled time-share conveyancing for the First Group throughout South Africa. His particular areas are land assembly through consolidation and subdivision, the opening of township registers, and sectional-title establishment and transfer.
Karl has also completed training in mediation, co-mediation and alternative dispute resolution, which he uses to resolve disputes without protracted litigation.

name: Jacques de Villiers
qualifications: BA, LLB, LLM (Planning, Development & Environmental Law), Certificate in Government Contracts & Procurement Law, Remote Mediation Foundation Training
membership: Legal Practice Council, Environmental Law Association, Association of Arbitrators (Southern Africa) NPC
projects: Legal advisor to the PropSol and PropWatch joint ventures and to KwaDukuza Municipality’s Ease of Doing Business project. Has served on Municipal Planning Tribunals and appeal panels throughout KwaZulu-Natal.
bio: Jacques holds a BA and an LLB from Rhodes University and a Master of Laws in Environmental Law from the University of KwaZulu-Natal, where his thesis examined the Spatial Planning and Land Use Management Act (SPLUMA) and its effect on public service infrastructure, with particular attention to sections 29 and 30. He is admitted as an attorney of the High Court of South Africa.

He is one of the legal advisors to the PropWatch and PropSol joint ventures, the GeoAfrika-led property portfolio service providers to SANRAL, where he works on aligning SANRAL’s planning and infrastructure development with SPLUMA. He also handles state property management matters, including expropriation disputes and compliance with expropriation procedures.
Jacques has trained in mediation and alternative dispute resolution, and is working on ways to bring both into development legislation and processes for private and public development projects.

name: Fuad Davids
qualifications: LLB, LLM (Environmental Law), ADR, Safety, Health, Environment and Quality (SHEQ) Representative, PG.Dip Climate Change and Energy Law
membership: Legal Practice Council, Environmental Law Association, Association of Arbitrators (Southern Africa) NPC
projects: Legal advisor on the panels of the KZN Department of Economic Development, Tourism and Environmental Affairs (EDTEA), Transnet, Dube TradePort Corporation and other local authorities in KwaZulu-Natal and the Western Cape. Also assists private developers with environmental compliance and litigation.
bio: Fuad holds an LLB from the University of the Western Cape, obtained in 2016, and was admitted as an attorney of the High Court of South Africa in 2018. He completed a Master of Laws in Environmental Law at the same university in 2021, researching the use of criminal sanctions in prosecuting environmental crimes.
He joined HSG in 2021, transferring from the Western Cape, and heads the environmental law and litigation departments.
In 2022 Fuad completed a Postgraduate Diploma in Climate Change and Energy Law. He has a particular interest in renewable energy and infrastructure projects.

name: Tess Coetzee
bio: Tess holds an LLB from UNISA, obtained in 2010. She was admitted as an attorney in February 2013 and as a conveyancer in April 2023, and has the right of appearance in the Magistrates’ Court, the High Court, the Supreme Court of Appeal and the Constitutional Court.
She leads the conveyancing department in the firm’s Western Cape office. Her wider experience covers legal costs, taxation, deceased estates and litigation.
Tess provides legal-costs services to state departments and law firms, has trained other organisations in that field, and has served on several legal-costs panels.

name: Matthew Bremner
qualifications: BS Sci. (Politics, Law & Philosophy), LLB, LLM, (Environmental Law), Legal Education and Development
bio: Matthew holds a Bachelor of Social Science in Politics and Philosophy, an LLB, and a Master of Laws in Environmental Law, for which his thesis considered carbon tax and its effectiveness in promoting environmental conservation. He was admitted as an attorney of the High Court of South Africa in 2015.

He acts for individuals, businesses, construction companies, property developers and government institutions, and has appeared at levels from the Magistrates’ Court to the Constitutional Court, as well as regularly presenting matters to government committees.
Matthew’s work covers litigation, town planning law, environmental law, petroleum law, property law, administrative law and construction law.

name: Warda Jones
qualifications: LLB, Conveyancer, Notary Public, Professional Legal Training
bio: Warda holds an LLB from the University of KwaZulu-Natal. She was admitted as an attorney and conveyancer in 2014 and as a notary in 2016.

Her practice is in conveyancing and notarial work, which she handles from instruction to registration for individual, commercial, developer and estate-agent clients, and on low-cost housing projects. She has worked on several banking panels for conveyancing and bond registration, including Islamic and shariah bonds, and has acted in private, commercial and state transactions.
Warda also supports and trains the firm’s candidate attorneys who are working towards their conveyancing and notarial admissions.

name: Lusiwe Phungula
qualifications: Bachelor of Laws (LLB), Practical Legal Training (PLT)
bio: Lusiwe was admitted as an attorney of the High Court in 2023 and she holds an LLB degree from the University of the Free State, which she completed in 2020. She is currently pursuing a National Diploma in Real Estate at CPUT.

At HSG, Lusiwe’s primary focus lies in property law, specifically handling matters related to debt collection, evictions, and land claims. She actively engages with both landowners and tenants, working to resolve disputes and, when necessary, take court action. Additionally, Lusiwe provides valuable advice on property and contract matters, ensuring compliance with policies and legal standards. In her multifaceted legal journey, Lusiwe remains dedicated to navigating the intricate landscape of property law, advocating for clients, and ensuring adherence to legal norms

name: Jane Tennet
membership: Memberships: Environmental Law Association, EAPASA, IAIAsa  Associations: Association of Arbitrators Southern Africa NPC
projects: Jane has worked on various projects in the environmental sphere including:  Royal Palm Property Holdings | Palm Lakes Estates: ECO and environmental development advice  Owetu Owabo Engineers | Sakuma Engineers: Bhekezulu Water Reticulation Project, EIA and ECO First Group: EIA’s for the La Montagne Northern Walkway and Beach Walkway PropWatch JV | SANRAL: environmental compliance assessments, and advice for various leased properties  Dube Tradeport Corporation: Environmental Legal consulting
bio: Jane Tennet has completed a BA Environmental Management through the University of South Africa (UNISA) in 2020 and an honors degree in Development Studies in 2023. Having worked extensively at HSG, Jane has gained valuable experience in various areas such as property administration, project management, land acquisition, and land legal matters. She is also an integral part of the environmental section, where she serves as the firm’s environmental consultant.

In her role, Jane works closely with clients to help them meet their environmental impact requirements while also providing valuable support to the environmental law sector. She is registered with IAIASA, as a Candidate EAP through EAPASA and with the ELA. Her unique insights and experience make her an invaluable member of the HSG team, contributing to property, development, and environmental practice and legislation at the firm.

name: Mahendren Pillay
position: Assistant Illegal Occupations and Land Invasions Manager
